_comment: Blueprint background modules. The field behind the tiles is drawn as an engineering drawing: graph paper, scale ticks, corner registration, and the app wordmark. A blueprint module supplies the *geometry* of that drawing; a theme supplies its *ink* (blueprint.accent / blueprint.ink vary per theme), so one blueprint reads warm on a light theme and cold on a dark one. Add a module here and it appears in the view tile's field picker: nothing else needs touching.

graph.name: Graph paper
graph.note: 5 mm engineering squares: a hairline minor grid, a ruled major grid every five, and a long tick every twenty-five.

iso.name: Isometric
iso.note: 30° drafting triangles: the same rules rotated into two mirrored shears, so clusters sit on a lattice.

dot.name: Dot matrix
dot.note: The quiet one: punched dots with a single ruled major grid, for reading long documents.

plate.name: Blue plate
plate.note: A full drawing plate: heavier major rules, a border, corner registration marks, and a title block.

void.name: Deep field
void.note: No drawing: the field keeps only its bloom, vignette and grain.

resolve.note: minorDefault is the minor cell in world px at zoom 1; every other step is derived from it, so a blueprint never needs more than one number of its own.
